title: Lior and the Cipher
premise: Lior Iversen, a true-crime podcaster who has spent seven years cataloging the unsolved disappearance of a local girl, receives two anonymous letters in one week: one confessing to the crime, one promising the truth is still buried. As Lior investigates the letters' origins, they uncover a cipher hidden in their late mother's belongings, revealing that the case touches their own family — and that the confessor is someone in their found family of case archivists. The climax forces Lior to decode the cipher publicly, exposing the killer and the town's complicity, and in the aftermath Lior finally claims a name and identity that were never theirs to inherit.
about_author: Vesper Quintana is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging cold-case files in small-town New England before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the paperwork of grief and the families we assemble from shared secrets.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Handwriting
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. On the seventh anniversary of the Marlowe girl's disappearance, Lior receives a confession letter and, days later, a second letter from the same hand promising 'more where that came from.' Lior's emotional beat: the thrill of a lifetime colliding with dread that the letters are bait — or a mirror.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior revisits their meticulously organized case archive and interviews the three core volunteers of their podcast community — retired deputy Halloran, librarian June, and teenage superfan Theo — testing each against the confession's details. One detail in the letter matches something never made public.

chapters.title: What Mother Filed Under M
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Sorting their late mother's estate, Lior finds a box of clippings about the Marlowe case — and a page of odd numeric notations that look like a cipher. The emotional beat: the first crack in Lior's belief that their family stood outside the story.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Lior and an unnamed letter-writer. The writer describes watching Lior at the archive, intimate and patient, while Lior receives a third letter: a partial key to the cipher. Rising tension — the correspondent knows Lior's routines better than Lior does.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Swore
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior tracks down the original lead detective, now dying, who admits the case was closed under pressure from families who 'needed it closed.' He warns Lior that the cipher's notation style matches police interview summaries. Emotional beat: institutional betrayal.

chapters.title: Found Family, Found Suspects
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with Theo's interlude. Lior quietly investigates Halloran, June, and Theo, hating every minute. Theo, feeling the suspicion, digs independently and finds the cipher references a location — the old boathouse. The found family begins fracturing under the weight of doubt.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Key
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the boathouse, Lior finds evidence the girl never left town — and a fresh footprint. Someone else has been there recently, and recently means since the letters began. The emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve; the case is live again.

chapters.title: Decoding the Inheritance
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Working through the night, Lior fully decodes the cipher: it's their mother's hand, documenting what she witnessed the night of the disappearance — and naming the killer. The final entry is unfinished, cut off mid-sentence. Grief and fury fuse into purpose.

chapters.title: The Last Recording
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, climax. Lior stages a live episode reading the decoded confession aloud, forcing the killer — Halloran, who silenced Lior's mother to protect the town's respectable men — to come for the archive. Theo and June arrive; the confrontation is recorded, and the truth goes out on air.

chapters.title: Lior, Signed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, resolution. In the aftermath, the town reels, the case reopens and closes properly, and Lior buries their mother's file for good. Lior signs off the final episode under their chosen name, keeping the found family that survived the truth. Emotional beat: identity claimed, inheritance rewritten.
